samples.text: It applies to the international system and it applies to Europe. We will not abandon the European idea because the European path has been difficult. The European Union remains for us our natural, political, economical, and institutional home. and we have to work to do at home. We must strengthen the rule of law, build more effective institutions, build a more competitive economy and strengthen our citizens' confidence in their own state. That is our responsibility and we will not shift it to Brussels. At the same time, we expect European integration to remain a merit-based process based on measurable criteria, not a process in which bilateral issues can continually move the goalposts. We are not asking for an easier path. We are asking for a path governed by rules. We are not asking for lower standards. We are asking for standards to remain standards. This is equally important for Europe's credibility at a time when its geopolitical weight will increasingly depend on its ability to translate its commitments into the tangible political outcome and on its resolve to uphold the values it exposes and to remain steadfast in advancing them despite the many challenges it face. Excellencies, The future international order will not be shaped only on battlefields or in diplomatic halls. It will be also shaped in laboratories, in schools, in factories, in energy grids, in data centers, and in the ability of societies to make sense of the changes that technology is bringing. Artificial intelligence is not longer a subject of the future. It is infrastructure for today, for the present. Today, the world is once again recognizing the values of resilience, of reliable energy, of infrastructure, of diversified transport routes, of nearby and trusted supply chains. For us, the intensified development of Corridor 8 and Corridor 10 is a part of broader European vision to better connect the Adriatic, Ionian, the Black Sea, the Asian, and Central Europe.

Electricity grids, energy, and digital corridors, ports, and shipping routes are levers of power. Geography matters. And our ambition is to translate our unique position into stronger links between Europe, the Middle East, the Gulf, and North Africa. Therefore, we are investing in a new generation of connectivity projects, such as GREGY, which will bring clean energy from Egypt to Europe, and the Great Sea Interconnector, which will connect European electricity grids with Cyprus and Israel. At the same time, we leverage our unique geographic positions to become a provider of energy security to our northern neighbors. And as the Prime Minister of a leading shipping nation, it is worth remembering a stark fact. More than 90% of global trade is conducted by sea. If we systematically threaten the freedom of navigation and do not protect vital sea routes, the global economy risks coming to a grinding halt. And this is something that should be of great interest to every single country represented in this great assembly. Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to conclude with a few thoughts on the topic of artificial intelligence. One of my favorite bands when I was growing up was Talking Heads. And little did I know that the time that David Byrne iconic song, we are on a road to nowhere would ring so prescient four decades later. For the first time, for the first time in the history of our species, we have created a technology that openly challenges the supremacy of the human mind as the pinnacle of our evolutionary development. I will not dwell on the positive transformational potential of this revolutionary technology. whether in disease eradication, productivity enhancement, or fighting climate change. However, it is simply impossible to ignore the fact that at present, the risks of an unchecked and unregulated advance in artificial intelligence could greatly outweigh its potential benefits.

Let me conclude by addressing briefly two issues critical to our shared future: the advent of artificial intelligence (AI) and the adverse effects of digital technology, especially on our children and our teenagers.
